items.title: 18.10.2 Reaction of Manganate(VII) Ion with Iron(II) Ion

source_refs.note: Topic 18.10.2 (PDF 34). The printed E of -0.77 V, the E cell of +2.29 V and the overall equation are corrected (Quick Check 18.8 itself gives +0.77 V). Flagged for review.

blocks.text: In this reaction MnO4- is reduced and Fe2+ is oxidised. The half-reactions, written as reductions, are:

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book prints E = -0.77 V for Fe3+ + e- -> Fe2+; the standard value is +0.77 V, as the book's own Quick Check 18.8 gives.
Combine and balance the two equations and sum up their standard electrode potentials so that we can check feasibility of the overall reaction.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Correct working: written as an oxidation, 5 x [Fe2+ -> Fe3+ + e-] has E = -0.77 V. The balanced overall equation is MnO4- + 8H+ + 5Fe2+ -> Mn2+ + 5Fe3+ + 4H2O (the book leaves out 8H+ and prints 5Fe2+ among the products). E cell = 1.52 - 0.77 = +0.75 V, so the reaction is feasible.
The positive value of the standard electrode potential indicates that this reaction will proceed to the right, making this reaction feasible.
